findings.evidence: `pkg/session/session.go:2386` returns `(nil, true, err)` on `finishStmt` error after `drs.TryDetach()` and closing `detachedRS` (`return nil, true, err` at `pkg/session/session.go:2415`). `pkg/server/internal/resultset/resultset.go:148` propagates the `detached` flag even when `err != nil` (`return nil, detached, err` at `pkg/server/internal/resultset/resultset.go:155-156`). But `pkg/server/conn_stmt.go:437` drops `ok` on error (`if !ok || err != nil { return false, err }` at `pkg/server/conn_stmt.go:439-441`), and `pkg/server/conn_stmt.go:349` ignores `err` whenever `ok` is false (falls back to eager). Test expectation confirms `detached==true` on `finishStmt` error: `pkg/executor/staticrecordset/integration_test.go:216` enables `finishStmtError` and asserts `ok==true` with non-nil error.
findings.fix: In `executeWithLazyCursor`, preserve the detach flag on error (e.g. `if !ok { return false, nil } ; if err != nil { return ok, err }`) and/or make `executeWithCursor` treat any non-nil `err` from the lazy attempt as fatal (no eager fallback) when the RS might already be detached.
findings.impact: If `TryDetach` reports `detached==true` with an error (e.g. commit/cleanup failure in `finishStmt`), the server can silently drop that error and proceed into eager cursor fetch using an RS that the session layer explicitly marks as unusable. This risks incorrect protocol/statement outcomes (error swallowed), double-finish/cleanup, or panics/errors when iterating a no-longer-valid RS.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master@b75374faa619e24e380292fdbdf0f6fe5bf11943`: `pkg/server/conn_stmt.go` still has `if !ok || err != nil { return false, err }` in `executeWithLazyCursor` and `executeWithCursor` still ignores `err` when `ok==false`.
findings.verify: Add a server-level test that enables `github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/session/finishStmtError`, turns `tidb_enable_lazy_cursor_fetch=ON`, executes a cursor statement, and asserts COM_STMT_EXECUTE returns the injected error and does not attempt eager cursor execution; also assert statement/cursor is reset and no further FETCH is possible.
findings.what: Lazy-cursor path drops `TryDetach`’s `detached` flag on error, so `finishStmt`/detach errors can be swallowed and the server may incorrectly fall back to eager cursor execution on an RS that the session layer says is no longer usable.

findings.evidence: `pkg/session/session.go:2402` creates `cursorHandle := ...NewCursor(...)` and wraps it into `crs`, but on `finishStmt` error it only closes `detachedRS` and returns (`pkg/session/session.go:2409-2416`) without `cursorHandle.Close()`. `pkg/session/cursor/tracker.go:41` stores new cursors in a `sync.Map`, and `pkg/session/cursor/tracker.go:85` shows the only removal path is `Handle.Close()`. Cursor presence affects global min start TS reporting: `pkg/executor/staticrecordset/integration_test.go:179` verifies minStartTS stays pinned until the cursor-backed recordset is closed.
findings.fix: In `execStmtResult.TryDetach`, ensure `cursorHandle.Close()` is called on the `finishStmt` error path (e.g. `cursorHandle := ...; if err != nil { cursorHandle.Close(); detachedRS.Close(); ... }`).
findings.impact: On `finishStmt` failure during detachment, the session leaks a cursor handle in the tracker; this can leak memory/IDs and can pin `MinStartTS` (GC safepoint protection) longer than intended, potentially blocking GC advancement and causing storage bloat if the session continues running.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master@b75374faa619e24e380292fdbdf0f6fe5bf11943`: `pkg/session/session.go` still returns on `finishStmt` error without closing the created `cursorHandle`.
findings.verify: Extend `pkg/executor/staticrecordset/integration_test.go:216` to assert the cursor tracker is empty after `TryDetach()` returns error (or add a new test that ranges cursors and expects none), ensuring no leaked cursor handle on the error path.
findings.what: `execStmtResult.TryDetach` leaks a cursor handle when `finishStmt` fails (creates a cursor, but doesn’t close it on error), which can pin `MinStartTS`/GC and leak cursor-tracker entries.

subject: server: add protocol support for lazy cursor fetch (#54527)
summary: Reviewed `afd6d6a33a` vs first parent with focus on executor/session/sessionctx interactions for lazy cursor detachment. Found two High-severity error-path issues: (1) the server lazy-cursor wrapper drops `TryDetach`’s `detached` flag on error, so detach/`finishStmt` failures can be swallowed and incorrectly fall back; (2) `execStmtResult.TryDetach` creates a cursor handle but doesn’t close it if `finishStmt` fails, potentially leaking and pinning `MinStartTS`/GC. Both issues remain present on `upstream/master`.
